ir5_usyears.topic: Netanyahu's American years and pre-1992 warnings

claims.text: Netanyahu took a BS in architecture and an MS in management studies at MIT; worked at Boston Consulting Group from 1976 (Writers Directory: consultant 1976-78); organized international conferences on terrorism in Jerusalem (1979) and Washington (1984); deputy chief of mission in Washington from 1982 under Ambassador Moshe Arens; UN ambassador four years from 1984; returned 1988 and was elected to the Knesset

Sources differ on the Jonathan Institute's founding (1976, 1977, 1980); Writers Directory lists him as executive director 1978-80; before Washington he was a manager at the Jerusalem furniture maker Rim (1980-82); MIT master's dated 1976

The Jonathan Institute's 1979 Jerusalem conference was attended by future President George H.W. Bush and representatives of AEI, CSIS and Commentary; the 1984 Washington follow-up emphasised 'the relationship between Islam and terror'; Netanyahu framed terrorism as part of a struggle 'between the forces of civilization and the forces of barbarism'

Terrorism: How the West Can Win (1986, ed. Netanyahu) argued international terrorism 'poses a mortal danger to civilized society', was sustained by 'terrorist states', 'most notably Syria, Libya, Iran, and South Yemen', with the Soviet Union and satellites behind the network; the NYRB review does not mention nuclear weapons

Undated video excerpt (Grabien, headlined 1986): Netanyahu said that if such regimes believed they could act freely 'you may very well find yourself in a world in a few years from now with a Gaddafi or Khomeini with nuclear weapons'; the Khomeini reference places it before June 1989; date and venue not established

ir5_predictions.topic: Netanyahu's dated Iran nuclear predictions 2009-2026 and the record that followed

claims.text: UNGA 27 Sep 2012 (transcript): 'by next spring, at most by next summer, at current enrichment rates' Iran would finish medium enrichment; 'From there it's only a few months, possibly a few weeks' before enough enriched uranium for the first bomb; Iran '70% of the way there'; 'A red line should be drawn right here'
Ynet's report of the delivered speech: 'By next summer, at current enrichment rates, they will have finished the medium enrichment'; 'Red lines don't lead to war, red lines prevent war'
Meet the Press, 16 Sep 2012: Iran 'six month away from being about 90 percent of having the enriched uranium for an atom bomb'

Congress, 3 Mar 2015: the deal 'doesn't block Iran's path to the bomb; it paves Iran's path to the bomb'; would 'all but guarantee' Iran gets nuclear weapons; more than four dozen Democrats said in advance they would not attend; Biden abroad; Obama said the speech contained nothing new

13 June 2025 video statement: Iran had 'enough highly enriched uranium for nine atom bombs' and took 'steps to weaponize'; 'if not stopped, Iran could produce a nuclear weapon in a very short time. It could be a year. It could be within a few months, less than a year'
24 June 2025: Netanyahu: 'For decades, I have promised you that Iran would not have nuclear weapons'

IAEA Board, 12 June 2025: 19-3-11 resolution found Iran not complying with safeguards obligations, citing failures since 2019 and unexplained uranium traces at undeclared sites; first such finding in nearly two decades; Iran said it 'has no technical and legal basis' and announced a new enrichment facility
Grossi, 19 June 2025 (Al Jazeera interview): 'We did not find in Iran elements to indicate that there is an active, systematic plan to build a nuclear weapon'

IAEA GOV/2015/68, 2 Dec 2015: activities relevant to a nuclear explosive device conducted 'prior to the end of 2003 as a coordinated effort'; some after 2003; 'did not advance beyond feasibility and scientific studies'; no credible indications after 2009
IAEA 1 May 2018, after Netanyahu's archive presentation: the Board had declared its consideration of the issue closed (Dec 2015)

29 Dec 2025 Mar-a-Lago: Netanyahu discussed possible 2026 strikes, Iran's nuclear status and especially its missile programme; no bomb timeline reported; US official: 'the tension will be in agreeing what reconstitution means'
28 Feb 2026 statement: aim to 'remove the existential threat' posed by the regime; Iran 'must never be allowed to arm itself with nuclear weapons'; no timeline given

AP 22 June 2026: Netanyahu: 'Had we not acted in Operation Rising Lion and then in Operation Roaring Lion, Iran would have had atomic bombs'; AP: Iran was 'months or years away' from a usable weapon before the wars, no evidence it chose to build one; IAEA inspections have not reported evidence of a weapons programme; Grossi: stockpile could allow as many as 10 bombs if Iran chose

Ynet 17 Sep 2026: an anonymous senior Israeli official said the 'weaponization group was very far from developing a nuclear weapon' and Iran had no authorization to break out; IAEA estimate 440.9 kg of 60% uranium as of 13 June 2025; account not independently verifiable

AP Jan 2011 (citing Yedioth): departing Mossad chief Meir Dagan said Iran would not be able to build a bomb before 2015, the programme delayed by unspecified 'measures', and Israel 'should not hurry to attack'; government spokesman declined comment
Hadley quoted the 2007 NIE: Iran's 2003 halt was 'directed primarily in response to increasing international scrutiny and pressure'
